name: Calvin Coolidge
summary: Coolidge was a Republican small-government conservative who favored low taxes, balanced budgets, a protective tariff, restricted immigration and light business regulation. He defended constitutional limits, representative government and obedience to law, supported women's suffrage and federal action against lynching, and kept the US out of the League of Nations while backing the World Court and the Kellogg-Briand pact.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said the government should avoid artificial price support and let economic laws operate; held that business profit is the only basis for wages and employment.

public-ownership.rationale: Opposed government ownership of coal mines, urged sale of the government merchant fleet to private owners and of Muscle Shoals, and said public ownership cannot distribute wealth.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Urged cutting the surtaxes on large incomes, arguing that high rates yield less revenue and discourage investment; signed the 1926 act that reduced them.

unions-good.rationale: Mixed: as governor he signed laws protecting trade unions and said organized labor's gains came through public opinion, but he opposed the Boston police union and said strikes divide the community.

property-fundamental.rationale: Said the Constitution guarantees the right to hold property, great and small, and that the people's title to it is absolute; but put rights of persons first.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Held that regulation exists so business may be free rather than hampered; the anti-trust laws punish unlawful purpose, not size. His administration's regulation was light.

cut-welfare.rationale: Contested: opposed relief that pauperizes ('breed not mendicants, but men') yet backed mothers' aid, veterans' care and federal welfare work.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Backed prohibition of narcotics and intoxicating liquors as public-health law and called it his duty to enforce Prohibition.

state-harmful.rationale: Described government as the people's agent whose proper role is limited, yet defended it as the means of liberty and order.

empower-police-military.rationale: Told Congress in 1923 that the Army and Navy should be strengthened rather than weakened, and urged a stronger Coast Guard for Prohibition enforcement.

decide-locally.rationale: Said education is peculiarly local and that racial difficulties are best worked out by communities; warned against centralization of power in Washington.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wrote that education not based on religion and character is not education and wished for the advancement of religion, while rejecting religious tests for office.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Urged federal anti-lynching law, funded Black vocational and medical education, signed Indian citizenship; but left most racial problems to local communities.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said 'America must be kept American' and urged being intensely and scrupulously American.

gradual-change.rationale: Held that there is far more danger of harm than hope of good in radical changes to institutions, and valued tradition and custom.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Signed the 1924 Immigration Act, said conditions warranted a limitation of those admitted, and later called the law beneficial and protective of wage earners.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Refused to join the League of Nations and wanted no obligations restricting freedom of action; supported only the World Court with reservations.

free-trade.rationale: Rejected free trade in favour of the protective tariff, which he said saves the American market for American workmen.

nation-first.rationale: Mixed: said the country attends to its own affairs and protects its citizens, yet recognizes an obligation to help others and backed arbitration and the Kellogg pact.

open-borders.rationale: Signed the 1924 immigration law and repeatedly urged a policy of restricted immigration.

central-planning.rationale: Warned that paternalism and bureaucratic supervision of every activity kill initiative; rejected socialism and public ownership.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Welcomed the 1926 act restoring estate-tax rates to 'more reasonable figures' and hoped the federal estate tax would withdraw in favour of state inheritance taxes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In his 1923, 1926 and 1927 annual messages and 1925 inaugural he credited the protective tariff with high wages and prosperity and defended it as a standing policy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Contrasted a system of divine right of rulers by inheritance, where he said there is no real freedom, with self-government.

democracy-best.rationale: Said that people's political mistakes, however grave, are unimportant compared with those of every kind of autocracy (Evanston, 1923).

direct-votes.rationale: Said the Founders created a republic rather than a pure democracy and that the essence of a republic is representative government.

natural-rulers.rationale: Held that if no one is born into a superior station there is no ruling class and authority must rest on the people.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said government cannot guarantee a successful life or relieve people of the results of their own folly, and that rewards of industry belong to those who earn them.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Said any attempt to maintain rights without observing duties is a contradiction of terms and that the duty of obedience needs more emphasis.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Said employment and wages depend on someone making a profit, which is the sound basis of distribution; denying profit denies the reward of thrift.

taxation-theft.rationale: Called taxes not needed for public necessity 'a species of legalized larceny' but accepted that tax ministering to public necessity is constitutional, so he did not treat taxation itself as theft.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Held that rigid economy and surpluses, applied to debt retirement and tax cuts, remedy economic ills better than government spending; championed the budget system.

class-collaboration.rationale: Said industry cannot flourish if labor languishes and that employer and workman must each contribute; warned strikes embitter and divide the nation into warring classes.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Wanted arrivals limited to capacity to absorb them into good citizenship; said those who do not want to be partakers of the American spirit ought not to settle here.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Favored limited government and economy but backed waterways, flood control, education aid, a welfare department, regulation and radio licensing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said the rights of colored citizens are as sacred as any other's, and that the standard applied to inhabitants is manhood, not place of birth.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Called it final that governments derive their just powers from the consent of the governed.

separated-powers.rationale: Credited the three independent branches with checks on each other as the guarantees of liberty.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Said the country could not barter away its independence or sovereignty even while joining the World Court.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Favored the long-established custom against a third presidential term, and held that one man can hardly serve the country well beyond eight years.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said policy avoids permanent political alliances that sacrifice independence, while having no alliance to end.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Opposed cancelling war debts owed to the United States, calling repayment a moral obligation, while accepting adjustment of terms; debtors were European states.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Said owners of property are charged with a service and that these duties carry divine sanction, though he also called property title absolute.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Argued that governments do not make ideals but ideals make governments, and that the Declaration grew from religious teaching.

ban-cartels.rationale: Called the anti-trust laws sound in theory and said unlawful assemblages of wealth may be dispersed, as a mob is; as a legislator he helped draft a bill against local price-cutting to injure rivals.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Said free government must not degenerate into the unrestrained authority of a mere majority, and that the Declaration's rights cannot be destroyed by any majority.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Stated that no one is born into a superior station and there is to be no ruling class.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Said the country extended its domain over distant islands and accepted an obligation to bestow justice and liberty on less favored peoples.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Held that the Constitution's guaranties can be changed only by amendment with the consent of the States, and praised them as protection of liberty.

elective-rulers.rationale: Said the people have the right to choose their own rulers and that no one has any right to rule over another.

office-by-exam.rationale: Urged extending the classified merit system for federal employees and preferred it to the spoils system.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Championed the federal budget system and called Congress jealous of its prerogative; approval of budget by Congress is implied.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Taught that obedience to law is the first duty of a citizen and that more emphasis must be placed on it, starting in the home and school.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Credited industry and enterprise with creating national wealth, attracting immigration and driving progress, and defended the profit system.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Asked whether any prosperity or commercial instrument can be too great, and argued wealth is the product of industry; condemned only wealth assembled for unlawful purposes.

racial-pride.rationale: Wished false and ignorant prejudice to be replaced with a 'true and enlightened pride of race'.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Said the nation looks with disfavor on all aggressive warfare and backed the Kellogg-Briand pact, while keeping marines in Nicaragua to protect citizens' interests.

arms-reduction.rationale: Backed the Washington naval limitation treaty and wanted further agreements to reduce the waste of armament competition, while insisting on adequate defense.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wanted railroad labor relations to keep systematic collective bargaining with conciliation and voluntary arbitration, and urged a mediation board for coal disputes.

farm-price-support.rationale: Vetoed the McNary-Haugen farm relief bill in 1927 and 1928 as government price fixing that would create a bureaucracy.

women-suffrage.rationale: As a Massachusetts legislator he supported a woman suffrage resolution and later cited it as becoming law; he endorsed women's role in public life.

notes: As governor he backed hours and wage laws for women and opposed child labor; as president he held that such matters were for the states, and favored a child-labor amendment only in 1923. Many economic and social topics are unanswered because he left them unaddressed.
